key_insight: Placing trainable nonlinear functions on physical connections lets analogue neural networks solve smooth continuous-control problems more efficiently than standard multilayer perceptrons.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a path to ultra-low-power hardware for robotics and energy systems, with projected CMOS operation around 30 microwatts and direct transfer to analogue hardware at scale.
method: Implemented trainable nonlinear connection functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Compared performance on smooth targets such as robotic kinematics, continuous control, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking.
Also reproduced the approach in memristive simulation to isolate the architectural benefit from any single device type.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardware transfer across approximately 35,000 connections with quantified fidelity, and shows fewer nodes and connections than MLPs on smooth regression-style tasks but not on classification-like boundaries.
watch_item: The advantage is task-dependent, so the approach may not reduce parameters or improve efficiency for decision-boundary-heavy classification problems.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
